name: The Falconer’s Comet
image_style: Illuminated-manuscript-inspired gouache with finely inked contours, restrained medieval marginalia geometry, and subtle astronomical chart textures; reverent historical atmosphere, dry wit, tactile paper grain, and softly weathered pigments. Use an unusual palette of near-black aubergine, bone parchment, oxidized turquoise, muted vermilion, and tarnished brass, with controlled contrast and broad uncluttered shadow shapes. Keep the upper edge spacious and visually quiet, with one calm region suitable for desktop widgets. No lettering, logos, watermarks, frames, or interface elements.
scene: A moonlit 13th-century Crusader castle courtyard rendered with architectural and historical accuracy: a solemn falconer in period dress gently tends a hooded peregrine beside a stone cistern, while distant banners and battlements recede into the night. Space Ghost stands respectfully at the edge of the courtyard in his muscular white costume, black hood and mask, yellow cape, and red power bands, rigidly presenting a tiny ceremonial falcon perch as though receiving an important military inspection. The falconer remains dignified and mildly puzzled; the sacred Christian context is treated reverently, with a small chapel visible in the background but never used as a prop or punchline. Place the figures low in the composition, leaving a broad tranquil star-dark upper sky and a calm shadowed corner for widgets. Exactly one striking 16:10 landscape wallpaper, no text or lettering.
